newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BOKSIC AND BALBO RELIVE DERBY DAYS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BOKSIC AND BALBO RELIVE DERBY DAYS.

text.p: When Croat striker Alen Boksic left Lazio for Juventus last summer, the Rome club's coach Zdenek Zeman summed up his verdict.
"Boksic has great qualities and potential," the Bohemian said. "But he never showed them in Rome."

The words may come back to haunt Zeman but Lazio's arch-rivals Roma test the water first on Saturday when the 26-year-old is set to return to his former home ground for the first time with European champions Juventus.
His main rival will be Roma's Argentine striker Abel Balbo, veteran derby opponent for the past three years.
Both first arrived in Rome in 1993, the Argentine closing the season with 12 goals. Boksic scored just four.
In 1994-95, Balbo was runner-up scorer in the league with 22 behind his compatriot Gabriel Batistuta on 26.
Boksic, overshadowed at a club boasting one of Italy's leading marksmen in Giuseppe Signori, hit nine.
After falling out more than once with Zeman, failing to click with Signori either on or off the pitch and being laid off by injury, the Croat packed his bags and headed north.
Over at Roma it was the coach who left. Veteran Carlo Mazzone was replaced by Argentine Carlos Bianchi in a move that only made Balbo more at home than ever.
Many thought Lazio had done well to replace their malcontent with Italian Igor Protti, signed from Bari after he shared last season's goalscoring honours with Signori.
The word filtering out from Rome was that Boksic, who replaced Gianluca Vialli when the striker left for Chelsea, was difficult. His reputation is somewhat different now.
"Watching him play is truly a pleasure for the eyes," declared La Gazzetta dello Sport this week, describing the fast and powerful player as emblematic of the new Juve.
Under coach Marcello Lippi, he has scored two match-winning goals for Juventus in the Champions' League and another two for Croatia in a World Cup qualifier.
Balbo, a quiet Argentine who leads the life of a model professional and keeps his name out of the gossip columns, has scored four times in six league games this season.
But where Boksic's confidence is high, Balbo leads a troubled team at Roma after two straight defeats.
"Now I'm playing better because I'm physically more comfortable," Boksic said this week. "Zeman was massacring me with his methods, as all the injuries I got showed."
Zeman, as strong-willed as the player and just as plain-spoken, replied that if Boksic had trained better he would probably not have had a problem.
Juventus owner Giovanni Agnelli is an admirer of his newcomer, saying that Boksic evokes memories of Poland's Zbigniew Boniek who played for the club in the 1980s.
The similarities with Boniek are accentuated by the fact that the Croat plays alongside French international Zinedine Zidane - - recalling Juve's Michel Platini-Boniek duo.

Agnelli use to say that Boniek was "bello di notte "-- beautiful by night -- in a joking reference to the Pole's propensity to score in floodlit European Cup matches while frequently missing in daylight league games.
Boksic, the truck driver's son from Split, has been behaving similarly this season. Roma, who host Juventus under floodlights, had better watch out.
